description: Root-isolation certificate for the Trump octic (A03; Ellsworth 2023): p(x) = x^8 - 20x^7 + 178x^6 - 842x^5 + 1923x^4 - 496x^3 - 6754x^2 + 12420x - 6865. Discharges checklist S3 / A62 finding F7: s-hat is THE unique root of p in [3877083/1000000, 3877084/1000000], and it is the SECOND (largest) of exactly two real roots of p.

taylor_shift_at_a.description: Coefficients d_k of p(a + t) = sum d_k t^k, a = 3877083/1000000. d_0 = p(a) < 0; d_1..d_8 are ALL POSITIVE, so p is strictly increasing on [a, +inf) by pure algebra (for 0 <= u < v: p(a+v) - p(a+u) = sum_{k>=1} d_k (v^k - u^k) > 0). This is the fact the Lean discharge of shat_spec uses (no calculus, no Sturm chain needed inside Lean).

verification.checker: certs/verify_sturm.py (exact rational arithmetic, Python stdlib fractions only; recomputes the Sturm chain, all sign-variation counts, the Taylor shift, and every claim above from the polynomial alone)
verification.lean: lean/PackingCertMathlib/PackingCertMathlib/TopLevel.lean: shat is a definition (Classical choice on the unique root) and shat_spec a THEOREM as of A63; the Lean proof uses IVT for existence and the all-positive Taylor shift for uniqueness
verification.method: Sturm's theorem: number of distinct real roots of p in (x1, x2] = V(x1) - V(x2) where V(x) = sign variations of the Sturm chain p_0 = p, p_1 = p', p_{i+1} = -rem(p_{i-1}, p_i); counts at -inf/+inf from leading coefficients. p is squarefree iff the chain terminates at a nonzero constant (it does: gcd(p, p') is constant).
